plan: 2 Kings 20:1-11; Isaiah 38:1-8; 2 Chronicles 32:24-31; Isaiah 38:9-22; 2 Kings 20:12-19; Isaiah 39:1-8

readings.title: Hezekiah's Illness and Miraculous Healing
readings.subtitle: The Prophet Isaiah delivers a death sentence, but Hezekiah's prayer results in a 15-year extension of his life and a sign of the shadow moving backward.
readings.text: [2 Kings 20:1] In those days Ḥizqiyahu was sick unto death. And Yeshayahu the prophet, son of Amots, went to him and said to him, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Command your house, for you are going to die, and not live.’</dq> ” [2] And he turned his face toward the wall, and prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, [3] “<dn>I</dn> pray to <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, remember how <dn>I</dn> have walked before <dn>You</dn> in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done <dn>את</dn> what was good in <dn>Your</dn> eyes.” And Ḥizqiyahu wept bitterly. [4] And it came to be, before Yeshayahu had gone out into the middle court, that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to him, saying, [5] <dq>“Return and say to <dn>את</dn> Ḥizqiyahu the leader of <dn>My</dn> people, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Daviḏ your father, “<dn>I</dn> have heard your prayer, <dn>I</dn> have seen your tears. See, <dn>I</dn> am going to heal you. On the third day go up to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [6] “And <dn>I</dn> shall add to your days fifteen years, and deliver <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> this city from the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur, and shall defend <dn>את</dn> this city for <dn>My</dn> own sake, and for the sake of Daviḏ <dn>My</dn> servant.” ’ ”</dq> [7] And Yeshayahu said, “Take a cake of figs.” And they took and laid it on the boil, and he recovered. [8] And Ḥizqiyahu said to Yeshayahu, “What is the sign that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does heal me, and that <dn>I</dn> shall go up to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the third day?” [9] And Yeshayahu said, “This is the sign for you from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does <dn>את</dn> the word which <dn>He</dn> has spoken: shall the shadow go forward ten degrees or go backward ten degrees?” [10] And Ḥizqiyahu said, “It would be easy for the shadow to go down ten degrees; no, but let the shadow go backward ten degrees.” [11] And Yeshayahu the prophet cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> brought the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down on the sundial of Aḥaz.

readings.title: Isaiah's Account of Hezekiah's Healing
readings.subtitle: A parallel account of Hezekiah's sickness, his prayer, and YeHoVaH's promise to heal him and give him a sign.
readings.text: [Isaiah 38:1] In those days Ḥizqiyahu was sick and near death. And Yeshayahu the prophet, the son of Amots, came to him, and said to him, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Command your house, for you are going to die and not live.’</dq> ” [2] And Ḥizqiyahu turned his face toward the wall, and prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [3] and said, “<dn>I</dn> pray, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, please remember how <dn>I</dn> have walked before <dn>You</dn> in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done <dn>את</dn> what is good in <dn>Your</dn> eyes.” And Ḥizqiyahu wept bitterly. [4] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yeshayahu, saying, [5] <dq>“Go and say to Ḥizqiyahu, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Daviḏ your father, “<dn>I</dn> have heard your prayer, <dn>I</dn> have seen your tears. See, <dn>I</dn> am adding fifteen years to your days. [6] “And out of the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur <dn>I</dn> shall deliver <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> this city, and protect <dn>את</dn> this city.” ’ [7] “And this is the sign to you from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does <dn>את</dn> this word which <dn>He</dn> has spoken: [8] “See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing <dn>את</dn> the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down with the sun on the sundial of Aḥaz, ten degrees backward.”</dq> And the sun returned ten degrees on the dial by which it had gone down.

readings.title: Hezekiah's Song of Gratitude
readings.subtitle: After his recovery, Hezekiah writes a psalm reflecting on his brush with death and praising YeHoVaH for delivering him from the pit.
readings.text: [Isaiah 38:9] This is the writing of Ḥizqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, when he had been sick and had recovered from his sickness: [10] <dn>I</dn> said, “Am <dn>I</dn> to go into the gates of She’ol in the prime of <dn>my</dn> life? Shall <dn>I</dn> be deprived of the rest of <dn>my</dn> years?” [11] <dn>I</dn> said, “<dn>I</dn> shall not see <dn>Yah</dn> – <dn>Yah</dn> in the land of the living! <dn>I</dn> shall no longer look on man with the inhabitants of the world! [12] “<dn>My</dn> dwelling is plucked up, taken from me like a shepherd’s tent. <dn>I</dn> have cut off <dn>my</dn> life like a weaver; <dn>He</dn> cuts me off from the loom. From day to night <dn>You</dn> make an end of me. [13] “<dn>I</dn> soothed myself until morning. Like a lion, so <dn>He</dn> shatters all <dn>my</dn> bones. From day to night <dn>You</dn> make an end of me. [14] “Like a swallow or a thrush, so <dn>I</dn> chattered; <dn>I</dn> moaned like a dove; <dn>my</dn> eyes look weakly on high. O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>I</dn> am oppressed, undertake for me! [15] “What do <dn>I</dn> say? For <dn>He</dn> has spoken to me, and <dn>He</dn> Himself has acted. Softly <dn>I</dn> go, all <dn>my</dn> years, because of the bitterness of <dn>my</dn> being. [16] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, by these do men live, and <dn>my</dn> spirit finds life in all of them. Restore me and make me live. [17] “See, for peace <dn>I</dn> had what was bitter, bitter. But <dn>You</dn> have lovingly delivered <dn>my</dn> being from the pit of corruption, for <dn>You</dn> have cast <dn>את</dn> all <dn>my</dn> sins behind <dn>Your</dn> back. [18] “For She’ol does not thank <dn>You</dn>, nor death praise <dn>You</dn>; those who go down to the pit do not watch for <dn>Your</dn> truth. [19] “The living, the living – he is praising <dn>You</dn>, as <dn>I</dn> do this day. A father makes known <dn>Your</dn> truth to his children. [20] “Come <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to save me! And let us sing <dn>my</dn> songs with stringed instruments all the days of our life in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [21] For Yeshayahu had said, “Let them take a cake of figs, and apply it on the boil, so that he lives.” [22] And Ḥizqiyahu asked, “What is the sign that <dn>I</dn> go up to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?”

readings.title: The Babylonian Envoys and Hezekiah's Folly
readings.subtitle: Hezekiah proudly displays his wealth to messengers from Babylon, prompting Isaiah to prophesy the future Babylonian captivity.
readings.text: [2 Kings 20:12] At that time Beroḏaḵ-Balaḏan son of Balaḏan, sovereign of Baḇel, sent letters and a present to Ḥizqiyahu, for he heard that Ḥizqiyahu had been sick. [13] And Ḥizqiyahu listened to them, and showed them <dn>את</dn> all his treasure house, <dn>את</dn> the silver and <dn>את</dn> the gold, and <dn>את</dn> the spices and <dn>את</dn> the precious ointment, and <dn>את</dn> all his armoury, and <dn>את</dn> all that was found among his treasures. There was not an object in his house or in all his rule that Ḥizqiyahu did not show them. [14] And Yeshayahu the prophet came to Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu, and said to him, “What did these men say, and from where did they come to you?” And Ḥizqiyahu said, “They came from a distant land, from Baḇel.” [15] And he said, “What have they seen in your house?” And Ḥizqiyahu answered, “They saw all that is in my house; there is not an object among my treasures that <dn>I</dn> did not show them.” [16] And Yeshayahu said to Ḥizqiyahu, “Hear the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: [17] <dq>See, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and <dn>את</dn> what your fathers have treasured up until this day, shall be brought to Baḇel – no object is to be left,’</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [18] <dq>And they are going to take away some of your sons who are to be born to you, whom you bring forth, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the sovereign of Baḇel.’</dq> ” [19] And Ḥizqiyahu said to Yeshayahu, “The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which you have spoken is good!” And he said, “Is it not so, if peace and truth are to be in my days?”

readings.title: Isaiah's Account of the Babylonian Envoys
readings.subtitle: The prophet confronts Hezekiah for his pride, foretelling that all the treasures he displayed will be carried off to Babylon.
readings.text: [Isaiah 39:1] At that time Meroḏaḵ-Balaḏan son of Balaḏan, sovereign of Baḇel, sent letters and a present to Ḥizqiyahu, for he heard that he had been sick and had become strong. [2] And Ḥizqiyahu was pleased with them, and showed them <dn>את</dn> the house of his treasures, <dn>את</dn> the silver and <dn>את</dn> gold, <dn>את</dn> the spices and <dn>את</dn> precious ointment, and <dn>את</dn> all his armoury, and <dn>את</dn> all that was found among his treasures. There was not an object in his house or in all his rule that Ḥizqiyahu did not show them. [3] And Yeshayahu the prophet went to Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu, and said to him, “What did these men say, and from where did they come to you?” And Ḥizqiyahu said, “They came to me from a distant land, from Baḇel.” [4] And he said, “What have they seen in your house?” And Ḥizqiyahu said, “They have seen all that is in my house; there is not an object among my treasures that <dn>I</dn> did not show them.” [5] So Yeshayahu said to Ḥizqiyahu, “Hear the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts: [6] <dq>See, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and <dn>את</dn> what your fathers have stored up until this day, shall be taken away to Baḇel; not a matter shall be left,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [7] <dq>And they shall take some of your sons who are born to you, whom you bring forth. And they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the sovereign of Baḇel.’</dq> ” [8] And Ḥizqiyahu said to Yeshayahu, “The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which you have spoken is good!” And he said, “Because there is peace and truth in my days.”
